lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Concept model C: conditional probability and its definition

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: Group X: 12 successes, 8 failures. Find P(success | X).

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Two events have P(A) = 7/10, P(B) = 8/10, and P(A and B) = 57/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).

items.prompt: In a group of 67, 20 do activity A, 28 do activity B, and 4 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 9/12 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A survey table records: group X with 20 successes and 18 failures; group Y with 19 successes and 25 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
Two events have P(A) = 2/10, P(B) = 3/10, and P(A and B) = 7/100. Are A and B independent?
choices: No; the two events are mutually exclusive.
Yes; P(A and B) equals P(A)·P(B).
Yes; the two events cannot occur together.
No; P(A and B) differs from P(A)·P(B).

items.prompt: In a group of 56, 32 do activity A, 23 do activity B, and 18 do both. Find P(A or B) as a fraction in lowest terms.
An event has probability 2/9 on a single trial. Two independent trials are run. Find the probability of at least one success, as a fraction in lowest terms.
A survey table records: group X with 21 successes and 14 failures; group Y with 23 successes and 8 failures. Find P(success | group X) as a fraction in lowest terms.
